body: Memos of 19 Sep 2008 and 15 Oct 2008, written in the Lehman panic. Binary framing: 'I think the outlook has to be viewed as binary: will the world end or won't it? If you can't say yes, you have to say no and act accordingly' - if the world ends, nothing you did matters; if it doesn't and you didn't invest, 'we wouldn't have done our job.' Oaktree invested ~$400m a week from 18 Sep 2008 to year-end (~$6bn in distressed debt, $7.5bn firm-wide), buying senior debt at prices that would work even if companies were worth 'only one-quarter or one-third of what the buyout funds had just paid.' The CIO meeting where no scenario was 'too bad' convinced him 'little optimism was embodied in the prices.' Key lines: 'Skepticism and pessimism aren't synonymous. Skepticism calls for pessimism when optimism is excessive. But it also calls for optimism when pessimism is excessive'; in the third stage of a bear market 'everyone agrees things can only get worse', and 'the greater long-term risk probably lies in not investing.' Outcome (per Marks): S&P 500 fell to 735 in Feb 2009, -53% from its 2007 high of 1,549, then recovered. Actionable for India: in a crash, ask whether the system survives; if yes, buy senior/high-quality claims at prices that work in bad cases (2008, Mar-2020 analogues).
title: Marks Sep/Oct-2008 'Nobody Knows' + 'The Limits to Negativism': skepticism means doubting pessimism too

body: Form 4 is due within 2 business days of an insider trade (SOX). Codes: P open-market purchase, S open-market sale, A grant, M option exercise, F shares withheld for tax, G gift. Since the SEC's Rule 10b5-1 amendments (effective Feb-2023; Form 4 checkbox from Apr-2023) each Form 4 flags whether the trade was under a 10b5-1 plan, and directors/officers face a cooling-off of the later of 90 days or 2 business days after the 10-Q/10-K (max 120 days) before trading under a new plan. Most selling is diversification: e.g. our test on Apple (last 15 Form 4s to 19-Nov-2026) found 30 open-market sales by 7 insiders ($127M), 0 buys, and almost all flagged 10b5-1 - normal for a mega-cap. Evidence (Lakonishok-Lee 2001) says sales have little predictive power. Flags that DO matter: several insiders (3+) selling off-plan within ~30 days, CFO/GC selling ahead of results, newly adopted plans followed by quick sales, selling into a stock-funded acquisition or secondary, founders cutting stakes sharply, and Form 144 notices clustering. sec_fetch.py insider TICKER prints transactions, the 10b5-1 flag and a cluster detector.
title: Reading Form 4 selling: ignore routine 10b5-1 sales, flag off-plan clusters
